module_doc.doc:
Convert human-readable Temporal durations to one deterministic numeric value. A month needs a calendar anchor; repeating that decision across queues, retries and timeouts produces inconsistent answers.

Use milliseconds() for shared conversion and compare() for shared ordering. Calendar units use 2000-01-01, so this is deterministic mechanics rather than a business calendar. A timer may still reject years and months; a lease may require positive time. On hosts without Temporal, import the explicit polyfill first. Use the temporal ponyfill export when your own application wants a local Temporal value without changing globals.

module_doc.doc:
Install Temporal only when the host does not provide it.

Import this module first at an application entry point. It lets duration,
context, queue, pool and workflow code run on hosts without global Temporal.
Libraries keep this choice with the application; ordinary utility imports do
not install globals. Each Worker or process has its own global and needs its
own entry-point import. An existing native implementation is preserved.

module_doc.doc:
Use Temporal in an application without installing a global.

This ponyfill exports the complete temporal-polyfill implementation. It
works when the runtime has no Temporal and keeps globalThis unchanged. Import
the explicit polyfill subpath instead when other libraries use global Temporal.
